question: Does the Kronos K-line foundation model, used zero-shot, rank crypto perps by next-week return well enough to earn a net premium after costs, add something beyond plain momentum, and forecast volatility better than trailing realized volatility?
registration_note: Declared 2026-10-01 before any Kronos forecast was produced on our data. Kronos pre-training data ends June 2024 (arXiv 2508.02739); the published weights were uploaded once on 2025-06-30 and later commits only edit the README, so July 2024 onward is unseen by the model. Caveat: the authors evaluated from July 2024, so model design may be partly tuned on that window; a forward watch is the clean test. Zero-shot only: no fine-tuning on our data.

pins.weights_sha256: recorded at first download in research/kronos/pins.json

forecast.bars: MEXC 8h OHLCV (open, high, low, close, volume)
forecast.context: the 400 bars that opened before 00:00 UTC of the rebalance day (the last closes at 00:00)
forecast.predicted_return: predicted close of the 21st bar / last context close - 1
forecast.predicted_move: mean absolute predicted 8h log return over the 21 bars, x sqrt(21)
forecast.coin_eligibility: at least 400 bars of history before the rebalance day

test_window.rebalance: the strategy-zoo/multi-premia weekly grid (every 7th day of the daily index)

samples: 70 development coins and 60 untouched coins (multi-premia caches), evaluated separately and pooled; none of their post-June-2024 data is in Kronos's pre-training

books.K1_kronos_xs: cross-sectional: long the top quartile of predicted 7-day return, short the bottom quartile, 0.5 gross per side, weekly, 20 bps, funding proxy (run_xs machinery)
books.K1_reference_momentum: frozen 30-day/7-day XS momentum on the same coins and window (reference only)

diagnostics.rank_ic: per rebalance, Spearman correlation between predicted and realized 7-day return; reported as mean and t over rebalances
diagnostics.K2_volatility: per rebalance, Spearman correlation of predicted_move with realized 7-day absolute log return, versus the same correlation for trailing 30-day realized vol; Kronos is better if its mean correlation is higher on both samples

pass_rules.K1: pooled 130-coin book: mean > 0, Newey-West t >= 2, Sharpe > 0 in both halves of the window (split at 2025-08-07); AND on each sample separately Sharpe > 0; AND correlation with the reference momentum book below 0.7
pass_rules.blend_addition: descriptive: 4-leg blend (S1, S2, S3, K1) vs 3-leg over the window
pass_rules.K2: descriptive only (sizing changes would be a separate registration)

if_passed: register a forward watch (weekly, CPU on GitHub Actions); nothing promoted
